title: skills(issue-authoring): should review-fix-loop-cutoff's marker-origin trust model be hardened beyond body-sha256-unchanged?
body:
## Background

`skills/issue-authoring/references/contract.md`'s "Narrow auto-release exception (review-fix-loop-cutoff)" (shipped via #2864/#2877/#2891) triggers purely on the presence of the exact HTML marker `<!-- <marker-prefix>-authoring-defer-source: review-fix-loop-cutoff -->` in a target's body at Stage 1 publication time, verified only via `#2877`'s body-sha256-unchanged-since-acquire provenance check -- which confirms the body has not changed since acquire, not who wrote the marker or that a real `idd-review-triage.instructions.md` round-count cutoff actually occurred.

This design was a deliberate outcome of the 2026-09-10 hearing that created this exception (`idd-skill-loop-cutoff-2026-09-10` session record): the hearing scoped auto-release narrowly to a single carrying target and reused body-content-unchanged as the sole provenance signal, implicitly extending trust to whichever session performs Stage 1 authoring. Cryptographic or workflow-origin authentication of *who* placed the marker was not part of that decision.

#2972 (verified 2026-09-14 against a downstream adopter's review feedback) re-raises this exact question: an ordinary Stage 1 draft that happens to contain the same literal marker text (copied content, or authored for unrelated reasons) would satisfy the same condition and trigger auto-release without ever having gone through the actual round-count cutoff the exception exists for.

## Proposed change

This requires a fresh maintainer risk-tolerance call, not an autonomous fix, since it revisits a boundary the 2026-09-10 hearing already set deliberately. Options:

- **A -- keep as-is.** Body-content-unchanged remains the sole provenance signal, consistent with the original hearing's scope. Close as not planned; the theoretical gap is accepted.
- **B -- add a corroborating trace requirement.** Require a linked comment, a companion-emitted token, or similar evidence tracing back to an actual `idd-review-triage.instructions.md` round-count-cutoff event before the marker is honored, in addition to the existing body-sha256 check.
- **C -- other/hybrid** (e.g. a lighter-weight signal than B, such as requiring the marker to have been present since the target's very first published revision, not just "unchanged since acquire").

## Acceptance Criteria

- A maintainer decision is recorded on this issue (e.g. `Maintainer decision (Groom hearing, <date>): <resolution>`) selecting one of the options above or a variant.
- If a design/code change is chosen, a follow-up implementation issue is filed capturing the concrete change and its own acceptance criteria.

Refs #2972

## Groom decision

Maintainer decision (Groom hearing, 2026-09-15): choose option A and keep the current body-sha256-unchanged provenance model as-is. The 2026-09-10 hearing deliberately accepted this narrow trust boundary, and no new evidence here justifies reopening it. Close this issue as not planned.
